title: AP2 alternative path: verifying mandates and receipts in a dispute
summary: After the fact, a dispute verifier collects both mandates and both receipts, recomputes the hash bindings and checks each receipt reference. AP2 defines these checks but leaves retention, retrieval and adjudication to others.

steps.label: Checkout Mandate and Checkout Receipt
steps.detail: Either the Shopping Agent or the Merchant may supply them. Retention and retrieval are out of scope; the specification suggests a future lookup keyed on transaction_id.

steps.label: Payment Mandate and Payment Receipt
steps.detail: The Shopping Agent, Credential Provider, Network or Merchant Payment Processor may supply them.

steps.label: Verify the Checkout Mandate under the Merchant rules
steps.detail: Signature chain and, for an autonomous purchase, every open-mandate constraint.

failures.outcome: It cannot serve as evidence of what the user approved.

steps.label: Recompute the hash of the included checkout_jwt
steps.detail: The recomputed value must equal checkout_hash.

steps.label: Match the Checkout Receipt reference
steps.detail: The receipt reference must equal the hash of the closed Checkout Mandate, computed the same way as sd_hash.

steps.label: Verify the Payment Mandate with checkout_hash
steps.detail: Under the Merchant Payment Processor rules, using checkout_hash from the Checkout Mandate as the expected transaction_id.

steps.label: Match the Payment Receipt reference
steps.detail: The reference must equal the hash of the closed Payment Mandate. When every check passes, the mandates show what the user and each role saw. Liability is still decided by network rules.
